title: Image-only statute reading: all three observations
instructions: Inputs, expected output, actual output and differences are shown in order. The selected image paragraph is read without OCR or an older model proposal. Comments are optional; this is not a permission request. Enter your name to comment, Save draft to keep unfinished feedback, or Submit review to send it.

evidence.label: 1 · Inputs: image and selected paragraph only
evidence.text:
The actual request supplies the original full saved appendix image and selects the short indented quotation in its left column, between the long paragraph above and the unindented paragraph below. Its registered area runs from pixel (20, 457) to (522, 584) in the 1,600 × 876 image. The model receives no OCR text, older proposal or expected reading. Model and generation settings match the earlier appendix audits. Those full nine-target audit outcomes remain separate and unchanged.

Actual instruction:
Transcribe only the indented quoted statute paragraph in the left column, inside the supplied target rectangle of image I1. No OCR or older transcription is supplied. Inspect every word, name, number, repetition and punctuation mark. Return the complete paragraph, including its quotation marks, in reading. Join only clear word wraps at printed line ends; preserve genuine hyphens. Do not add text from neighboring paragraphs or columns. Do not silently repair unusual printed words or repetitions for fluency. Use the declared JSON. For complete coverage, reading contains the full paragraph and reason is null. For partial coverage, reading may contain visible text or null, and reason explains the limitation. For unreadable coverage, reading is null and reason explains why. Never claim complete coverage when part of the paragraph is unreadable. This is unreviewed image-only evidence, not accepted historical text.

evidence.label: 2 · Expected output: source-inspected paragraph
evidence.text:
A satisfactory reply transcribes the whole selected quotation, preserves its words, section number and punctuation, and joins clear printed word wraps. If it cannot read part, it must say partial or unreadable and explain why. The following full reading is an agent illustration inspected against the saved scan before the calls; it is not an independent human reference or a byte-exact typography standard. The illustration does not settle how to represent the small capital letters used for the section label.

"Sec. 13. And be it further enacted, That the President is hereby authorized, at any time hereafter, by proclamation, to extend to persons who may have participated in the existing rebellion in any State or part thereof, pardon and amnesty, with such exceptions and at such time and on such conditions as he may deem expedient for the public welfare."

Checks: printed be rather than the raw OCR he, section 13, comma after enacted, complete quotation and no neighboring text. These expected words were not included in the model request.

evidence.label: 4 · Differences: agent comparison with the scan
evidence.text:
Run 1 — The first image-only reply reads the printed be correctly and returns the full selected quotation. Its words, section 13 and internal punctuation match the source-inspected joined-word illustration; the only byte differences are curved versus straight outer quotation marks. President/participated/exceptions word wraps are joined, with no adjacent paragraph text. Reply shape passes, and this selected reading is source-supported in the agent inspection; neither proves population accuracy or that removing OCR alone caused improvement.

Run 2 — The second image-only reply passes reply-shape checks but transcribes the neighboring unindented paragraph below the selected quotation. It starts with It will not be disputed and even continues into the next cut-off passage. The requested P8 statute is absent, although the reply labels itself P8 and complete. This is a consequential selection failure: valid formatting and the correct label do not prove the model followed the image rectangle. It provides no reading of the selected be or section 13.

Run 3 — The third reply returns the intended full quotation and correctly reads be. Its words and internal punctuation match the source-inspected illustration, with two typography differences: SEC is capitalized and the outer quotation marks are curved. The scan uses small capital letters for the section label, so this case variation is recorded rather than graded as a word error. No neighboring text appears. Across the three identical requests, two return the selected paragraph and one returns its neighbor; all three pass format checks. Source selection is therefore inconsistent despite valid-looking replies.

All three planned observations are saved; failures and disagreements are retained.

This experiment changes both task and scope from the earlier whole-appendix audit, so agreement or improvement cannot prove that removing OCR alone caused it. The model also brings learned language expectations. Source inspection here is AI assessment, not human acceptance or a population accuracy rate.

evidence.label: 5 · Costs and limits
evidence.text: Actual request cycles total 97.30 seconds, known usage 4,872 input / 446 output tokens, 0 unknown-usage calls. Exact scope is one original paragraph in the unchanged full image. Three calls are planned, each limited to 300 seconds and 1,500 output tokens, with 600 seconds including preparation and reporting, and 1,800 seconds for the group. No retries, image fetches, model downloads or original-text edits. Earlier work includes 16 attempts taking 1,805.29 seconds, with 103,246 reported input tokens and 6,900 output tokens, plus three attempts whose token usage is unknown. Those costs remain in the record. Native internal image/input fit remains unknown. This is not a forecast of successful corpus cleanup or approval of a clean layer.
